completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the register-bare/acquire-suffixed session-id defect in the three multi-task command files (research.md, plan.md, implement.md), which was causing every multi-task batch with a declared file_scope to self-refuse its own lock acquires. memory_candidates.content: When a static-guard grep test greps a file that ALSO contains an invariant-note explanation of the bad pattern it forbids (e.g. porting skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's own inline invariant comment, which necessarily mentions the forbidden suffixed-session_id string as an illustrative example), a naive flat grep -rnF for the bad substring across the whole file/tree will show false-positive hits. The correct guard scopes the grep to lines matching the actual call-site ERE first (e.g. `task-lock\.sh[[:space:]]+(acquire|release|heartbeat)`), then greps for the bad substring only within those matched lines. Don't be alarmed by a nonzero flat-grep count if the real regression guard is ERE-scoped this way -- verify against the actual guard mechanism, not a naive proxy sweep.

When check-extension-docs.sh reports multiple FAIL items after an edit, trace each one individually via git log/git show against the pre-edit commit before assuming it's caused by the current change. An index-entries.json line_count mismatch is only in-scope if git show against the immediately-preceding commit confirms the declared count matched the file's actual line count before this session's edits. Fix only the in-scope entry directly (surgical Edit), rather than running the bulk --write regeneration script, which would also silently correct unrelated, possibly-concurrent, out-of-scope entries in a shared multi-agent session.
